text.p: Ted Donato had a goal and an assist in a three-goal first period and Rob Tallas made 29 saves as the Boston Bruins held on to beat the New York Rangers 3-2 Sunday.
Barry Richter and Brett Harkins also scored in the first period for Boston, which has won three of its last four contests.
Tallas, who blanked Tampa Bay 3-0 on Saturday for his first NHL shutout, turned away all 10 shots he faced in the third period with a little help from teammate Don Sweeney.

With the Bruins holding a 3-2 edge and 13:45 remaining, Niklas Sundstrom's wrist shot from the slot squeezed under Tallas's arm. The puck was about to hit the goal line when Sweeney pulled it out and tucked it under Tallas.
"We were all excited coming in to play a team like the Rangers," Tallas said. "It makes it easy to get ready when you play a team like that, I know I was excited.

"I'm feeling confident. You have to give a lot of credit to the defence too. They've really been clearing the front out for me, like that play Sweeney made ... that's the second night in a row he's done something like that."

Tallas made two other excellent saves in the final period. He stopped Vladimir Vorobiev's partial breakaway with 11:44 left and stoned Brian Leetch on a one-timer from the bottom of the left faceoff circle with 3:20 to play.

"He's a gritty individual and a battler and tonight he made some big saves," Boston coach Steve Kasper said. "He came out of his net and challenged when he had to, controlled his rebounds well and he battled.
"The whole team just got an unbelievable boost on the bench that he was battling for us."

New York captain Mark Messier appeared to have a breakaway with 57 seconds remaining, but referee Kevin Collins ruled the pass crossed two lines. Replays showed that Boston's Ray Bourque deflected the puck, meaning the play was legal.
"I thought that Bourque tipped it," Tallas said. "I don't think he (Messier) heard the whistle, he didn't stop until I put my glove up and then looked back. I should try that in the future."
"It definitely hit one of their sticks, it was a mis-call, but it's tough to see everything out there," Messier said. "It's a disappointment, but what can you do?"
Vorobiev and Messier scored second-period goals and Leetch set up both scores for the Rangers, who dropped to 0-3-1 in their last four home games.
Glenn Healy made 27 saves and fell to 3-9-4. The Rangers have scored three goals or less in 13 of his 17 starts.
Boston defenceman Kyle McLaren suffered a separated right shoulder in the first period after he was hit by New York's Ulf Samuelsson.

In Anaheim, Keith Jones had a goal and two assists and Stephane Yelle broke a tie and sparked a three-goal third period by scoring 21 seconds in as the Colorado Avalanche cruised to a 5-2 victory over the Mighty Ducks.

Mike Ricci and Adam Deadmarsh each added a goal and an assist and Peter Forsberg set up two goals for the Avalanche, who stopped Anaheim's four-game home winning streak and won for the third time in four games.
Claude Lemieux scored his fourth goal in as many games and fourth of the season 91 seconds into the game to open the scoring for Colorado.
In Buffalo, Michal Grosek's goal with 4:41 left in regulation lifted the Sabres into a 2-2 tie with the sputtering Washington Capitals, who played without suspended star winger Peter Bondra.
Grosek got to a Garry Galley rebound at the bottom of the left faceoff circle and lifted the puck past goaltender Jim Carey.

The tying tally came 91 seconds after Steve Konowalchuk's power-play goal gave the Capitals their first lead of the game. Konowalchuk also assisted on Kelly Miller's goal for Washington, winless in five of its last six games (1-4-1).
Jason Dawe scored the other goal for for the Sabres, who went 4-2-1 on the longest homestand in franchise history and climbed within one point of first-place Pittsburgh in the Northeast Division.

In Detroit, Vyacheslav Kozlov used his backhand to swat a bouncing puck past Andy Moog 80 seconds into overtime as the Red Wings rallied from a two-goal deficit for a 4-3 victory over the Dallas Stars.
The Red Wings moved within five points of the first-place Stars in the Central Division and stopped an 0-4-2 home slide with their first win at Joe Louis Arena since the day after Christmas.
Steve Yzerman, Brendan Shanahan and Martin Lapointe also scored for Detroit, which allowed only 12 shots. Chris Osgood made just nine saves for the win.
Joe Nieuwendyk scored twice and Jamie Langenbrunner set up all three goals for the Stars, who suffered their second straight loss after a four-game winning streak.
